schemes.label: VAT registration number
schemes.helpText: UK VAT registration number of the supplier — format not fixed by the regulation itself (in practice GB followed by 9 digits, or 12 digits ending 000 for government departments/health authorities).

provenance.sourceText: The Value Added Tax Regulations 1995 (SI 1995/2518), regulation 14(1): "...a registered person providing a VAT invoice in accordance with regulation 13 shall state thereon the following particulars— (a) a sequential number based on one or more series which uniquely identifies the document, (b) the time of the supply, (c) the date of the issue of the document, (d) the name, address and registration number of the supplier, (e) the name and address of the person to whom the goods or services are supplied, ..."

schemes.notes: New for root TODO item 19 — no gb.json existed before this task (the removed compliance engine's own GB profile, git tag avant-refonte-documents, backend/src/compliance/profiles/data/gb.ts, was a 7-line noMandate() stub with no requiredIdentifiers at all — nothing to reuse from it). Fetched directly at legislation.gov.uk (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1995/2518/regulation/14, 2026-09-01). Reg. 14(1)(d) binds 'a registered person providing a VAT invoice' — i.e. it is the SUPPLIER's own registration number that a VAT invoice must show; it does not distinguish by legal form, so `appliesTo: 'BOTH'` (a UK sole trader/individual can be VAT-registered exactly as a company can). `required: false` because not every entity this catalog is asked about is itself a VAT-registered 'registered person' — a private consumer, or a business below/exempt from the VAT threshold, genuinely has no registration number to give, the same 'no per-entity VAT-registration-status input to condition on' reasoning `data/fr.json` and `data/de.json`'s own VAT entries in this catalog already use. No `pattern` is set, deliberately: reg. 14 requires 'the registration number' without specifying its shape anywhere in its own text, and this task did not find a primary/official text that does — https://www.gov.uk/vat-registration/vat-registration-number, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/vat-record-keeping, and two HMRC internal-manual URLs guessed for VAT invoice content all returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-01. The commonly-cited GB+9-digits (or GB+12-digits for government/health bodies) shape is real administrative practice, not something this task read at a primary source — left permissive rather than asserting an unsourced pattern, per this catalog's own no-invented-pattern discipline (schema.ts's header).

schemes.label: Companies House registered number
schemes.helpText: Companies House company number (commonly 8 digits, or 2 letters + 6 digits for Scottish/Northern Irish/LLP/overseas companies, e.g. SC123456, NI123456, OC123456) — exact format not found in a primary text during this task, see provenance.

provenance.resolutionNote: New for root TODO item 19 — as with the VAT scheme above, gb.ts at git tag avant-refonte-documents had nothing on identifiers to inherit. This task read two texts directly at legislation.gov.uk on 2026-09-01, and they point in different directions on the exact claim this scheme makes (a registered number on an INVOICE): (1) Companies Act 2006 s.82(1)-(2) (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2006/46/section/82) is a bare ENABLING power — 'The Secretary of State may by regulations make provision requiring companies— (a) to display specified information in specified locations, (b) to state specified information in specified descriptions of document or communication...' and '(2) The regulations— (a) must in every case require disclosure of the name of the company...' — it delegates the actual content rules to regulations and itself mandates only the NAME, never a number. (2) The regulations made under that power, The Company, Limited Liability Partnership and Business (Names and Trading Disclosures) Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/17), split the NAME and the NUMBER into two different rules with two different document lists: reg. 24(1) (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/17/regulation/24) requires the registered NAME on a long list that explicitly includes '(e) its bills of parcels, invoices and other demands for payment, receipts and letters of credit' — invoices are named outright here; but reg. 25(1)-(2)(b) (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/17/regulation/25) requires the registered NUMBER only on '(a) its business letters; (b) its order forms; and (c) its websites' — invoices are NOT in reg. 25's list, and nothing in reg. 25 extends it to reg. 24's list. So the read texts settle that a UK company's invoice must carry its registered NAME (a fact this catalog does not track — the frontend has no scheme for it), but do NOT settle that the invoice must carry the registered NUMBER (the LEGAL_ID fact this entry actually makes) — exactly the 'lettres commerciales ≠ factures' distinction this task was asked to watch for, mirrored by this same file's German counterpart (data/de.json's own LEGAL_ID entry, § 37a HGB). `appliesTo: 'COMPANY'` because both regulations bind 'every company' (a defined term under the Companies Act), not sole traders. The number's own FORMAT was separately searched for and not found in a primary/official text — https://developer-specs.company-information.service.gov.uk/guides/companyNumber, https://www.gov.uk/guidance/find-and-update-company-information, https://www.gov.uk/get-information-about-a-company and https://companieshouse.blog.gov.uk/2016/09/09/company-number/ were tried on 2026-09-01; only the last returned content and it did not describe the format. What would settle the required-on-invoice question: a source establishing that an invoice counts within reg. 25's 'business letters', or further regulation/case law extending reg. 25's particulars to reg. 24's document list. What would settle the format: an official Companies House publication (e.g. its API reference or a guidance page) spelling out the digit/letter-prefix rules directly.
